text: 天下为主，君为客
pinyin: tiān xià wéi zhǔ, jūn wéi kè
literal: the world · is · host, ruler · is · guest
natural: the people are the host, the ruler only a guest

meaning.en: Huang Zongxi's famous inversion: the realm and its people are what matter, and the ruler exists to serve them.
meaning.zh: 黄宗羲的名论：天下百姓才是根本，君主不过是为天下办事的客人。

equivalents: the people come first, the ruler last
government exists to serve the people

examples.zh: 黄宗羲说“天下为主，君为客”，把君民关系完全颠倒了过来。
examples.en: Huang Zongxi's 'the people are host, the ruler a guest' turned the relation between ruler and subject upside down.

examples.zh: 读《明夷待访录》，最让人震动的就是天下为主，君为客这句话。
examples.en: What strikes readers most in 'A Plan for the Prince' is the line 'the people are host, the ruler a guest'.

origin.source: 黄宗羲《明夷待访录·原君》

story.en: Huang Zongxi (1610-1695) wrote 'Waiting for the Dawn: A Plan for the Prince' (《明夷待访录》) after the fall of the Ming; in the chapter 'On the Ruler' (《原君》) he argues that rulers have turned the realm into private property.
story.zh: 黄宗羲（1610—1695）明亡后著《明夷待访录》，在《原君》篇中指出后世君主把天下当作一己的私产。

usage.en: Often quoted in discussions of early Chinese political thought. In the original the phrase reads 以天下为主，君为客; it is quoted here in the shortened form usual today.
usage.zh: 常在谈论中国古代政治思想时引用。原文作“以天下为主，君为客”，今天多引作此简略形式。

synonyms: 民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻

text: 为天下之大害者，君而已矣
pinyin: wèi tiān xià zhī dà hài zhě, jūn ér yǐ yǐ
literal: become · world · 's · great · harm · one, ruler · only · that's all
natural: the greatest scourge of the world is none other than the ruler

meaning.en: Huang Zongxi's blunt charge that the ruler himself, putting private gain first, is the realm's worst source of harm.
meaning.zh: 黄宗羲的尖锐批评：天下最大的祸害，正是只顾一己私利的君主。

equivalents: the ruler is the greatest evil of all
the tyrant is the people's worst enemy

examples.zh: 黄宗羲写下“为天下之大害者，君而已矣”，批判的是专制君主。
examples.en: Huang Zongxi wrote 'the greatest scourge of the world is the ruler alone', condemning despotic monarchs.

examples.zh: 课上老师引用“为天下之大害者，君而已矣”，讨论专制制度的弊端。
examples.en: The teacher quoted 'the ruler alone is the greatest scourge' to discuss the evils of autocracy.

origin.source: 黄宗羲《明夷待访录·原君》

story.en: In the chapter 'On the Ruler' Huang Zongxi concludes that those who bring the greatest harm to the world are the rulers themselves.
story.zh: 黄宗羲在《原君》篇中断言，给天下带来最大祸害的，正是君主自己。

usage.en: A strong, literary sentence in classical syntax (而已矣 = 'that is all'). Quoted in history and political-thought writing, usually together with 天下为主，君为客.
usage.zh: 文言句式，语气强烈（“而已矣”即“罢了”）。多见于历史和政治思想类文章，常与“天下为主，君为客”并引。

text: 六经责我开生面，七尺从天乞活埋
pinyin: liù jīng zé wǒ kāi shēng miàn, qī chǐ cóng tiān qǐ huó mái
literal: Six · Classics · charge · me · open · new · face, seven · feet · from · Heaven · beg · living · burial
natural: the Six Classics charge me to open a new face; my seven-foot frame begs Heaven for a living burial

meaning.en: Wang Fuzhi's self-written couplet: scholarship asks him to give the classics a fresh interpretation, while he resigns himself to burying his body, alive, in obscurity.
meaning.zh: 王夫之的自题联：经典要求他阐发出新的面貌，而他自己甘愿在乡野隐居中度过余生。

equivalents: called to renew the classics, content to be buried alive
a scholar's duty to the classics and his reclusive fate

examples.zh: 王夫之自题“六经责我开生面，七尺从天乞活埋”，表明了治学的抱负。
examples.en: Wang Fuzhi wrote 'the Six Classics charge me to open a new face; my frame begs Heaven for a living burial', declaring his scholarly ambition.

examples.zh: 这副对联“六经责我开生面，七尺从天乞活埋”常被拿来形容学者的使命感。
examples.en: The couplet 'the Six Classics charge me to open a new face, my frame begs Heaven for a living burial' is often used to describe a scholar's sense of mission.

story.en: Wang Fuzhi (1619-1692), who lived in seclusion in Hunan after the Ming collapse, is traditionally credited with this couplet written for his own portrait.
story.zh: 王夫之（1619—1692）明亡后隐居湖南著书，此联相传为他自题画像之作。

usage.en: Quoted for a scholar's sense of mission to renew learning, often with the tone of lonely perseverance. 开生面 means to open up a new aspect. The couplet is traditionally cited as Wang's own inscription for his portrait hall; the exact setting varies between accounts.
usage.zh: 常用来形容学者革新学问的使命感，带有孤独坚守的意味。“开生面”即开创新局面。此联一般认为是王夫之自题像堂联，具体场合各书说法略有出入。

text: 行己有耻，博学于文
pinyin: xíng jǐ yǒu chǐ, bó xué yú wén
literal: conduct · oneself · have · shame, broadly · learn · in · culture
natural: have a sense of shame in how you act, and learn broadly from culture

meaning.en: Gu Yanwu's summary of the scholar's way: keep a sense of shame in conduct and study widely in the classics and culture.
meaning.zh: 顾炎武对为学做人之道的概括：立身行事要有羞耻之心，求学要广博地学习文化典籍。

equivalents: have integrity and learn widely
conscience in conduct, breadth in learning

examples.zh: 校训刻着“行己有耻，博学于文”八个大字。
examples.en: The school motto, 'have a sense of shame in conduct, learn broadly from culture', is carved in large characters.

examples.zh: 他以行己有耻，博学于文作为座右铭。
examples.en: He took 'a sense of shame in conduct, broad learning in culture' as his personal motto.

story.en: In his 'Letter to a Friend on Learning' Gu Yanwu answers what the sage's way is: 'broad learning in culture' (博学于文) and 'a sense of shame in one's own conduct' (行己有耻).
story.zh: 顾炎武在《与友人论学书》中说，圣人之道，一曰“博学于文”，一曰“行己有耻”。

usage.en: Used as a motto for schools and scholars. Each half is also a Confucian phrase (行己有耻 from 《论语·子路》, 博学于文 from 《论语·雍也》); Gu Yanwu combined them as his summary of the sage's way. Gu Yanwu (1613-1682) is often counted among the late-Ming and early-Qing thinkers.
usage.zh: 常作学校和学者的格言。两句分别出自《论语·子路》《论语·雍也》，顾炎武将二者合起来概括圣人之道。顾炎武（1613—1682）是明末清初的重要思想家。

text: 有志者，事竟成，破釜沉舟，百二秦关终属楚；苦心人，天不负，卧薪尝胆，三千越甲可吞吴
pinyin: yǒu zhì zhě, shì jìng chéng, pò fǔ chén zhōu, bǎi èr qín guān zhōng shǔ chǔ, kǔ xīn rén, tiān bù fù, wò xīn cháng dǎn, sān qiān yuè jiǎ kě tūn wú
literal: have · will · person, matter · in the end · succeeds, smash · cauldrons · sink · boats, the hundred-and-two (Qin passes) · finally · belong to · Chu; painstaking · person, Heaven · not · fail, lie on brushwood · taste · gall, three thousand · Yue · armour · can · swallow · Wu
natural: where there's a will it succeeds: Xiang Yu smashed his cauldrons and Chu took the Qin passes; Heaven does not fail the diligent: Goujian tasted gall and Yue swallowed Wu

meaning.en: A famous couplet of encouragement: determination wins in the end, as Xiang Yu broke his cooking pots and sank his boats to take the Qin heartland, and Goujian slept on brushwood and tasted gall to conquer Wu.
meaning.zh: 著名的勉励对联：有志向的人终能成功，如项羽破釜沉舟而夺取秦地，勾践卧薪尝胆而灭掉吴国。

equivalents: where there's a will there's a way
perseverance pays off

examples.zh: 他把“有志者，事竟成，破釜沉舟，百二秦关终属楚；苦心人，天不负，卧薪尝胆，三千越甲可吞吴”写在书桌前，激励自己备考。
examples.en: He wrote the whole couplet 'where there is will, things succeed … Heaven does not fail the diligent …' above his desk to spur himself on for the exam.

examples.zh: 校长在毕业典礼上引用了“有志者，事竟成，破釜沉舟，百二秦关终属楚；苦心人，天不负，卧薪尝胆，三千越甲可吞吴”。
examples.en: The principal quoted the whole couplet 'where there is will, things succeed … Heaven does not fail the diligent …' at graduation.

usage.en: Traditionally credited to Pu Songling as a motto for himself, but the attribution is popular rather than documented, so no origin is given. Its opening is the common idiom 有志者事竟成, which already has its own entry; this entry is the whole couplet. 百二秦关 refers to the Qin heartland, defensible by 'two against a hundred'.
usage.zh: 相传为蒲松龄自勉联，但这一说法流传多于有据可查，故不标出处。开头的“有志者事竟成”已有单独词条，本条为完整对联。“百二秦关”指易守难攻的秦地关中。

text: 写鬼写妖高人一等，刺贪刺虐入骨三分
pinyin: xiě guǐ xiě yāo gāo rén yī děng, cì tān cì nüè rù gǔ sān fēn
literal: write · ghosts · write · demons · high · others · one · rank, stab · greed · stab · tyranny · enter · bone · three · parts
natural: his ghosts and demons outclass everyone's; his strikes at greed and cruelty cut three parts deep into the bone

meaning.en: Guo Moruo's couplet praising Pu Songling: his tales of ghosts and spirits are superior, and his satire of corruption and oppression bites deep.
meaning.zh: 郭沫若称赞蒲松龄的对联：他写鬼怪胜人一筹，讽刺贪官暴政入木三分。

equivalents: a master of the supernatural and of satire
satire that cuts to the bone

examples.zh: 郭沫若评价《聊斋志异》“写鬼写妖高人一等，刺贪刺虐入骨三分”。
examples.en: Guo Moruo judged 'Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio': 'his ghosts and demons outclass all others, his thrusts at greed and cruelty go deep'.

examples.zh: 蒲松龄故居的门口挂着“写鬼写妖高人一等，刺贪刺虐入骨三分”的对联。
examples.en: At Pu Songling's former home hangs the couplet 'his ghosts and demons outclass all others, his thrusts at greed and cruelty go deep'.

origin.source: 郭沫若题蒲松龄故居联（1962年）

story.en: Guo Moruo wrote the couplet for Pu Songling's former residence in Zibo, Shandong, in 1962.
story.zh: 1962年，郭沫若为山东淄博蒲松龄故居题写此联。

usage.en: A standard line of praise for Pu Songling and his 《聊斋志异》; 入骨三分 is itself a common phrase for incisive criticism. Guo Moruo (1892-1978) wrote it in 1962 for Pu's former residence in Zibo.
usage.zh: 常用来赞誉蒲松龄及其《聊斋志异》；“入骨三分”本身也是形容刻画、批评深刻的常用语。郭沫若（1892—1978）于1962年为淄博蒲松龄故居题写此联。

text: 天下古今之庸人，皆以一惰字致败；天下古今之才人，皆以一傲字致败
pinyin: tiān xià gǔ jīn zhī yōng rén, jiē yǐ yī duò zì zhì bài, tiān xià gǔ jīn zhī cái rén, jiē yǐ yī ào zì zhì bài
literal: world · ancient · modern · 's · mediocre · people, all · by · one · laziness · word · come to failure; world · ancient · modern · 's · talented · people, all · by · one · arrogance · word · come to failure
natural: in every age the mediocre fail through one word, laziness; the gifted fail through one word, pride

meaning.en: Zeng Guofan's warning: ordinary people are ruined by laziness, and talented people are ruined by arrogance.
meaning.zh: 曾国藩的告诫：普通人败于懒惰，有才能的人败于骄傲。

equivalents: the dull fail through sloth, the brilliant through pride
pride goes before a fall

examples.zh: 曾国藩说“天下古今之庸人，皆以一惰字致败；天下古今之才人，皆以一傲字致败”，这话对年轻人很有启发。
examples.en: Zeng Guofan said 'the mediocre fail through laziness, the gifted through pride', words that give young people much to think about.

examples.zh: 班主任把“天下古今之庸人，皆以一惰字致败；天下古今之才人，皆以一傲字致败”抄在黑板上。
examples.en: The class teacher copied 'the mediocre fail through laziness, the gifted through pride' onto the blackboard.

story.en: Zeng Guofan wrote letters of advice to his brothers and sons for decades, and this warning is traditionally traced to them.
story.zh: 曾国藩数十年间写给兄弟子侄的家书中多有训诫，此语一般认为出自其中。

usage.en: Widely quoted in self-improvement writing and in speeches to students. It is credited to Zeng Guofan (1811-1872), the Qing statesman and general, and is normally traced to his family letters and instructions; the wording varies slightly between published versions.
usage.zh: 常见于励志文章和对学生的讲话。一般认为出自清代政治家、军事家曾国藩（1811—1872）的家书家训，各种版本个别字句略有出入。

text: 物来顺应，未来不迎，当时不杂，既过不恋
pinyin: wù lái shùn yìng, wèi lái bù yíng, dāng shí bù zá, jì guò bù liàn
literal: things · come · accommodate, not yet come · not · go to meet, at the time · not · mix in, already past · not · cling
natural: meet what comes, do not go out to meet what has not; stay single-minded in the moment, and do not cling to what is past

meaning.en: A guide to a calm mind: respond to events as they arrive, do not worry in advance, concentrate on the task at hand, and do not dwell on the past.
meaning.zh: 一种心境修养：事情来了就顺势应对，不提前忧虑，做事时专心不杂，过去了就不留恋。

equivalents: live in the present
neither fret ahead nor dwell behind

examples.zh: 他把“物来顺应，未来不迎，当时不杂，既过不恋”当作处世的准则。
examples.en: He took 'respond to what comes, do not meet what has not come, stay focused now, do not cling to the past' as his rule for living.

examples.zh: 面对压力，不妨想想“物来顺应，未来不迎，当时不杂，既过不恋”。
examples.en: Under pressure, it helps to remember 'respond to what comes, do not meet what has not come, stay focused now, do not cling to the past'.

usage.en: Usually credited to Zeng Guofan as a rule of self-cultivation, and quoted in advice on equanimity. The attribution rests on later anthologies of his sayings and the ideas echo older Neo-Confucian and Daoist teaching, so no origin is given.
usage.zh: 一般认为是曾国藩的修身之语，常用于谈论平常心。这一归属主要见于后人汇编的语录，思想上也与宋明理学和道家的说法相通，故不标出处。

text: 花未全开月未圆
pinyin: huā wèi quán kāi yuè wèi yuán
literal: flowers · not yet · fully · bloom · moon · not yet · full
natural: flowers not yet fully open, the moon not yet full

meaning.en: The best moment is before completion: blossoms not fully open and a moon not yet full leave room for hope, so one should not seek perfection.
meaning.zh: 最美好的状态是未圆满之时：花未全开、月未全圆，还留有期待，不必追求十全十美。

equivalents: the best is yet to come
leave something to be desired

examples.zh: 曾国藩喜欢“花未全开月未圆”七个字，认为这是惜福的道理。
examples.en: Zeng Guofan loved the seven characters 'the flowers not yet fully open, the moon not yet full', seeing in them the way to cherish good fortune.

examples.zh: 人生不必求满，花未全开月未圆才最耐人寻味。
examples.en: Life need not be full: flowers not yet fully open and a moon not yet full leave the most to savour.

origin.source: 蔡襄《十三日吉祥院探花》

story.en: Cai Xiang (1012-1067) wrote the poem in 1066 while governing Hangzhou; the line was later much loved by Zeng Guofan.
story.zh: 蔡襄（1012—1067）于治平三年（1066年）知杭州时作此诗；这一句后来深受曾国藩喜爱。

usage.en: The line is by the Northern Song poet and calligrapher Cai Xiang (蔡襄), not Zeng Guofan. Zeng Guofan loved it and often quoted it as a lesson in cherishing fortune and keeping some room, which is why it is often linked with his name (and with his study name 求阙斋, 'Seeking Imperfection'). Quoted today to counsel against perfectionism.
usage.zh: 此句是北宋诗人、书法家蔡襄的诗句，并非曾国藩所作。曾国藩十分喜爱，常以它说明惜福、留有余地的道理，所以常与他联系在一起（也与他的书斋名“求阙斋”相呼应）。今天多用来劝人不要苛求完美。

text: 发上等愿，结中等缘，享下等福
pinyin: fā shàng děng yuàn, jié zhōng děng yuán, xiǎng xià děng fú
literal: make · top-grade · vows, form · middle-grade · ties, enjoy · low-grade · comfort
natural: aim for the highest vows, form ordinary ties, and enjoy only modest comforts

meaning.en: A life maxim: set the loftiest goals, mix with people on equal terms, and keep your own comforts modest.
meaning.zh: 一条人生格言：志向要立得最高，与人结缘不分高下，自己享受要知足节俭。

equivalents: aim high, live simply
think big, live small

examples.zh: 他一直信奉“发上等愿，结中等缘，享下等福”，生活简朴而志向远大。
examples.en: He always lived by 'make the highest vows, form ordinary ties, enjoy only modest comforts', frugal in life and lofty in aim.

examples.zh: 毕业赠言里，老师写下“发上等愿，结中等缘，享下等福”。
examples.en: In the graduation message the teacher wrote 'make the highest vows, form ordinary ties, enjoy modest comforts'.

usage.en: Popularly credited to the Qing statesman Zuo Zongtang (左宗棠) as a couplet he wrote for himself, and quoted as a motto. The attribution circulates widely but is not firmly documented (it is sometimes also given to Zeng Guofan), so no origin is given. Often quoted together with 择高处立，就平处坐，向宽处行.
usage.zh: 通常说是清代政治家左宗棠自题联，常用作格言。此说流传很广，但缺乏确凿文献（有时也说是曾国藩所作），故不标出处。常与“择高处立，就平处坐，向宽处行”并引。

text: 择高处立，就平处坐，向宽处行
pinyin: zé gāo chù lì, jiù píng chù zuò, xiàng kuān chù xíng
literal: choose · high · place · stand, settle · level · place · sit, toward · broad · place · walk
natural: stand on high ground, sit on level ground, walk the wide road

meaning.en: A life maxim: look from a high vantage, take a steady, humble seat, and always choose the broad path.
meaning.zh: 一条处世格言：站得高、看得远，坐得稳、不攀比，走路要选宽阔的大道。

equivalents: aim high, stay grounded, take the broad road
think big, sit tight, go wide

examples.zh: 他把“择高处立，就平处坐，向宽处行”贴在书房墙上。
examples.en: He pinned 'stand on high ground, sit on level ground, walk the wide road' on his study wall.

examples.zh: 创业之初，前辈送给他一句话：择高处立，就平处坐，向宽处行。
examples.en: As he started his business, an elder gave him one line: stand on high ground, sit on level ground, walk the wide road.

usage.en: Popularly credited to Zuo Zongtang (左宗棠) as part of a couplet he wrote for himself; it is the companion of 发上等愿，结中等缘，享下等福. The attribution is widespread but not firmly documented, so no origin is given.
usage.zh: 通常说是左宗棠自题联的一部分，与“发上等愿，结中等缘，享下等福”相配。此说流传很广，但缺乏确凿文献，故不标出处。

text: 新栽杨柳三千里，引得春风度玉关
pinyin: xīn zāi yáng liǔ sān qiān lǐ, yǐn dé chūn fēng dù yù guān
literal: newly · planted · poplars · willows · three thousand · li, draw · get · spring · wind · cross · Yumen Pass
natural: newly planted willows stretch three thousand li, drawing the spring breeze across Jade Gate Pass

meaning.en: A line praising the willows that Zuo Zongtang's army planted along the road to Xinjiang, so greening the arid northwest that spring itself seemed to pass the Jade Gate.
meaning.zh: 赞美左宗棠率军西征时沿途栽种杨柳之功：绵延数千里的绿荫，仿佛把春风引过了玉门关。

equivalents: greening the desert road
willows that bring spring to the frontier

examples.zh: 导游念起“新栽杨柳三千里，引得春风度玉关”，介绍起河西走廊的左公柳。
examples.en: The guide recited 'newly planted willows stretch three thousand li, drawing the spring breeze across Yumen Pass' as she introduced the Zuo willows of the Hexi Corridor.

examples.zh: “新栽杨柳三千里，引得春风度玉关”常被引用来赞美植树造林。
examples.en: 'Newly planted willows stretch three thousand li, drawing the spring breeze across Yumen Pass' is often quoted in praise of tree planting.

origin.source: 杨昌濬《恭诵左公西行甘棠》

story.en: Yang Changjun, a Hunan officer who served under Zuo Zongtang in the northwest, wrote the poem praising the willows planted on Zuo's campaign road; the line is its third and fourth.
story.zh: 杨昌濬曾随左宗棠在西北任职，作此诗赞美左军西征沿途所植杨柳；此二句为诗的后两句。

usage.en: Often quoted when speaking of Zuo Zongtang's campaign in the northwest and of afforestation. It plays on Wang Zhihuan's 春风不度玉门关 ('the spring breeze never crosses the Jade Gate'), turning it into its opposite. The willows are still called 左公柳.
usage.zh: 常在谈到左宗棠西征和植树造林时引用。此句反用王之涣“春风不度玉门关”之意。这些柳树至今仍被称为“左公柳”。

text: 鼓民力，开民智，新民德
pinyin: gǔ mín lì, kāi mín zhì, xīn mín dé
literal: stir · people's · strength, open · people's · intelligence, renew · people's · morals
natural: strengthen the people's bodies, open their minds, renew their morals

meaning.en: Yan Fu's three-part programme for national strength: build physical vigour, spread education and knowledge, and renew public morality.
meaning.zh: 严复提出的富强三纲：增强国民体质，开发国民智慧，更新国民道德。

equivalents: build up body, mind and morals
strengthen, educate and reform the people

examples.zh: 严复提出“鼓民力，开民智，新民德”，主张通过教育来救国。
examples.en: Yan Fu proposed 'strengthen the people's bodies, open their minds, renew their morals' to save the nation through education.

examples.zh: 教育史课程常以“鼓民力，开民智，新民德”概括严复的改革主张。
examples.en: History-of-education courses often sum up Yan Fu's reform ideas as 'strengthen the people's bodies, open their minds, renew their morals'.

story.en: Yan Fu wrote 'On Strength' (《原强》) in 1895, after China's defeat in the Sino-Japanese War, naming these three aims as the root of national strength.
story.zh: 1895年甲午战败后，严复作《原强》，提出这三点是国家富强的根本。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of late-Qing reform and education. 民力 is physical strength, 民智 intelligence and knowledge, 民德 morality. Yan Fu (1854-1921), the translator of Huxley and Adam Smith, set out the three aims in 1895.
usage.zh: 常在谈论晚清变法和教育时引用。民力指体力，民智指智识，民德指道德。严复（1854—1921）是赫胥黎、亚当·斯密著作的译者，1895年提出这三项主张。

text: 托古改制
pinyin: tuō gǔ gǎi zhì
literal: rely on · antiquity · reform · institutions
natural: reform by invoking the ancients

meaning.en: To press for reform by claiming ancient authority: presenting new ideas as the true teaching of the sages.
meaning.zh: 借助古代圣贤的权威来推行改革：把新主张说成是古人的本意。

equivalents: reform in the name of tradition
new wine in old bottles

examples.zh: 康有为托古改制，把孔子描绘成主张变法的改革者。
examples.en: Kang Youwei reformed by appealing to antiquity, portraying Confucius as a champion of change.

examples.zh: 这位领导托古改制，把新政说成是对传统的继承。
examples.en: The leader pursued reform in the name of the past, presenting the new policy as a continuation of tradition.

story.en: In 'Confucius as a Reformer' (《孔子改制考》) Kang Youwei argued that Confucius had himself invoked the ancient sage-kings to carry out reform; the book gave the Hundred Days' Reform its intellectual basis.
story.zh: 康有为在《孔子改制考》中论证孔子托称尧舜古制以改制，这一学说为戊戌变法提供了理论依据。

usage.en: Neutral, formal; used in history and political writing, and now also of any reform justified by appeal to tradition. It is the standard label for Kang Youwei's reform thought; the four characters are a later summary, while his own books argue the idea.
usage.zh: 中性，正式，多见于历史和政治论述，今天也可指借传统之名推行改革。它是概括康有为变法思想的通行说法；这四个字是后人的概括，康有为自己的著作论述了这一思想。

text: 不惜以今日之我难昔日之我
pinyin: bù xī yǐ jīn rì zhī wǒ nàn xī rì zhī wǒ
literal: not · spare · use · today · 's · self · challenge · yesterday · 's · self
natural: not hesitate to let today's self challenge yesterday's

meaning.en: Liang Qichao's description of his own habit: he did not shrink from contradicting and correcting his earlier views as his thinking developed.
meaning.zh: 梁启超对自己治学态度的自述：不惜用今天的认识去否定、纠正昨天的主张。

equivalents: not afraid to change one's mind
refute my former self

examples.zh: 科学家应当不惜以今日之我难昔日之我，不断修正自己的结论。
examples.en: A scientist should not hesitate to let today's self challenge yesterday's and keep revising conclusions.

examples.zh: 他写自传时坦然承认，自己是不惜以今日之我难昔日之我的人。
examples.en: Writing his memoir, he frankly admitted he was someone who never hesitated to let today's self challenge yesterday's.

story.en: In 'Intellectual Trends in the Qing Period' (《清代学术概论》, 1920) Liang Qichao says that he was not afraid to let 'today's self' challenge 'yesterday's self' as his views kept changing.
story.zh: 梁启超在《清代学术概论》（1920年）中自述，其思想屡变，不惜以“今日之我”难“昔日之我”。

usage.en: Quoted to praise intellectual honesty and willingness to revise one's views; 难 here is nàn, 'to challenge, to dispute'. Liang Qichao used it of his own shifting positions.
usage.zh: 用来称赞学术上的坦诚和勇于修正自己的看法；此处“难”读nàn，意为质难、驳难。梁启超以此自述其思想的转变。

text: 欲新一国之民，不可不先新一国之小说
pinyin: yù xīn yī guó zhī mín, bù kě bù xiān xīn yī guó zhī xiǎo shuō
literal: wish · renew · one · nation · 's · people, cannot · not · first · renew · one · nation · 's · fiction
natural: to renew a nation's people, one must first renew its fiction

meaning.en: Liang Qichao's claim that fiction shapes the mind of a people, so reform of the nation must begin with reform of its novels.
meaning.zh: 梁启超的主张：小说能塑造国民的精神，所以要革新国民，必须先革新小说。

equivalents: change the stories, change the nation
reform the people through reforming fiction

examples.zh: 梁启超提出“欲新一国之民，不可不先新一国之小说”，推动了小说界革命。
examples.en: Liang Qichao declared 'to renew a nation's people one must first renew its fiction', launching the 'fiction revolution'.

examples.zh: 文学史讲到晚清小说时，必会引用“欲新一国之民，不可不先新一国之小说”。
examples.en: Any lesson on late-Qing fiction is sure to quote 'to renew a nation's people one must first renew its fiction'.

origin.source: 梁启超《论小说与群治之关系》（1902年）

story.en: Liang Qichao opened the essay 'On the Relationship between Fiction and the Government of the People' in the journal 'New Fiction' (《新小说》) in 1902 with this line.
story.zh: 1902年，梁启超在《新小说》杂志发表《论小说与群治之关系》，以此句开篇。

usage.en: Quoted in literary history and in debates about the social role of literature. It is the opening of Liang's 1902 essay, a founding text of the late-Qing 'new fiction' movement.
usage.zh: 常见于文学史和关于文学社会功能的讨论。此句是梁启超1902年文章的开篇，是晚清“新小说”运动的奠基性文献。

text: 笔锋常带感情
pinyin: bǐ fēng cháng dài gǎn qíng
literal: pen · edge · often · carry · feeling
natural: a pen whose edge often carries feeling

meaning.en: Liang Qichao's description of his own 'new style' of prose: lucid in structure, with the writer's emotion often showing in the sweep of the brush.
meaning.zh: 梁启超对自己“新文体”的描述：条理清晰，行文中常常流露出作者的感情。

equivalents: writing charged with feeling
emotion in every stroke

examples.zh: 他的文章笔锋常带感情，读来让人热血沸腾。
examples.en: His essays are written with a pen that often carries feeling, and stir the blood.

examples.zh: 评论家称这位记者的报道笔锋常带感情。
examples.en: Critics said this reporter's pieces were written with a pen that often carries feeling.

story.en: In 'Intellectual Trends in the Qing Period' (《清代学术概论》) Liang Qichao describes his own 'new style' (新文体) as clear and well ordered, its pen often carrying emotion, with a special power over the reader.
story.zh: 梁启超在《清代学术概论》中评述自己的“新文体”：条理明晰，笔锋常带情感，对读者别有一种魔力。

usage.en: Used to describe persuasive, emotionally charged writing, especially journalism and essays. Liang's own text says 笔锋常带情感, and 笔锋常带感情 is the form usually quoted; both are given.
usage.zh: 用来形容有感染力、饱含情感的文章，尤其是新闻和议论文。梁启超原文作“笔锋常带情感”，通行引用多作“笔锋常带感情”，两种写法并列。

text: 各国变法，无不从流血而成
pinyin: gè guó biàn fǎ, wú bù cóng liú xuè ér chéng
literal: every · country · change · laws, none · not · from · shed · blood · and · succeed
natural: in every country, reform has been achieved only through bloodshed

meaning.en: Tan Sitong's remark that no country has reformed its system without bloodshed, and that China, where no one had yet died for reform, had not yet earned renewal.
meaning.zh: 谭嗣同的名言：各国变法都是流血牺牲换来的，而中国还没有为变法流血的人，所以国家不能昌盛。

equivalents: no reform without sacrifice
reform is written in blood

examples.zh: 谭嗣同说“各国变法，无不从流血而成”，决心以自己的牺牲唤醒国人。
examples.en: Tan Sitong said 'in every country reform has come through bloodshed', resolving to rouse the nation by his own sacrifice.

examples.zh: 历史老师引用“各国变法，无不从流血而成”来讲解戊戌变法的失败。
examples.en: The history teacher quoted 'in every country reform has come through bloodshed' to explain the failure of the Hundred Days' Reform.

origin.source: 梁启超《谭嗣同传》所记谭嗣同语（1898年）

story.en: Liang Qichao's biography records that, in September 1898 as the Hundred Days' Reform collapsed, Tan Sitong refused to flee and spoke these words to him before he was executed.
story.zh: 梁启超《谭嗣同传》记载，1898年9月戊戌变法失败时，谭嗣同拒绝出逃，对梁启超说了这番话，不久就义。

usage.en: Quoted about the 1898 Reform and political sacrifice. The words are known from Liang Qichao's biography of Tan, which records Tan's remark to him as the coup unfolded and continues: 'if there is any such case in China, let it begin with me'. A reported speech rather than Tan's own writing.
usage.zh: 常在谈论戊戌变法和政治牺牲时引用。此语见于梁启超所作《谭嗣同传》，记载政变发生时谭嗣同对梁启超所说的话，下文是“有之，请自嗣同始”。是转述的谈话，并非谭嗣同的自撰文字。

variants: 各国变法，无不从流血而成，今中国未闻有因变法而流血者，此国之所以不昌也；有之，请自嗣同始

text: 望门投止思张俭，忍死须臾待杜根
pinyin: wàng mén tóu zhǐ sī zhāng jiǎn, rěn sǐ xū yú dài dù gēn
literal: see · a door · seek · lodging · think of · Zhang Jian, endure · death · a moment · await · Du Gen
natural: at the sight of any door I seek shelter and think of Zhang Jian; I endure death a little longer, waiting for Du Gen

meaning.en: Opening couplet of Tan Sitong's prison poem: he thinks of the Han figures who sheltered a fugitive or survived to see justice, as he awaits death after the failed reform.
meaning.zh: 谭嗣同狱中诗的开头两句：想起汉代投宿逃亡的张俭和装死待机的杜根，表达变法失败后坦然等待就义的心情。

equivalents: an exile's thoughts of heroes of old
awaiting death with dignity

examples.zh: 课堂上，老师讲解了“望门投止思张俭，忍死须臾待杜根”的典故。
examples.en: In class the teacher explained the allusions in 'at every door I seek shelter, thinking of Zhang Jian; I endure death a little longer, waiting for Du Gen'.

examples.zh: 展览里陈列着谭嗣同的《狱中题壁》，开头便是“望门投止思张俭，忍死须臾待杜根”。
examples.en: The exhibition displays Tan Sitong's 'Written on the Prison Wall', which opens with 'at every door I seek shelter, thinking of Zhang Jian; I endure death a little longer, waiting for Du Gen'.

story.en: Tan Sitong wrote the poem on his prison wall in September 1898 after the failure of the Hundred Days' Reform, shortly before his execution.
story.zh: 1898年9月戊戌变法失败后，谭嗣同在狱中题写此诗，不久被害。

usage.en: From a poem of four lines; its famous end is 我自横刀向天笑，去留肝胆两昆仑. Zhang Jian and Du Gen were Eastern Han men persecuted by eunuchs: Zhang Jian fled and was sheltered by ordinary people; Du Gen, beaten and left for dead, feigned death and later survived. Literary; the poem's exact wording varies slightly between versions.
usage.zh: 出自一首四句诗，著名的结句是“我自横刀向天笑，去留肝胆两昆仑”。张俭、杜根都是东汉时受宦官迫害的人：张俭逃亡，得到百姓收留；杜根被杖击后装死得以脱身。文言，各版本字句略有出入。

text: 冲决网罗
pinyin: chōng jué wǎng luó
literal: burst · break through · net · snare
natural: burst through the nets

meaning.en: To smash through all the nets that bind people, meaning outworn customs, doctrines and authority.
meaning.zh: 冲破一切束缚人的网罗，指陈旧的习俗、教条和权威。

equivalents: break the shackles
burst the chains

examples.zh: 青年们要冲决网罗，追求思想的自由。
examples.en: Young people should burst through the nets and pursue freedom of thought.

examples.zh: 这部小说写的是一位女性冲决网罗、寻找自我的故事。
examples.en: The novel tells of a woman who bursts through every net to find herself.

story.en: In the preface to 'A Study of Benevolence' (《仁学》) Tan Sitong calls on readers to break through the nets of material gain, of pedantic scholarship, of all philosophical systems and of authority.
story.zh: 谭嗣同在《仁学》自叙中号召冲决利禄之网罗、俗学之网罗、群学之网罗，直至君主、伦常等一切网罗。

usage.en: Literary and rousing; used of breaking free of constraints in thought, custom or politics. Tan Sitong used it in the preface to 《仁学》 (1896-97) as a call to burst through the nets of profit-seeking, scholarly pedantry, and all doctrines.
usage.zh: 文言色彩，鼓动性强，用于冲破思想、习俗或政治上的束缚。谭嗣同在《仁学》自叙中用它号召冲破利禄、俗学和各种学说的网罗。
